benchmark_method.fixture: Two exact selected-round offsets of the algebraic rectangle, translated by (1/20, 1/40), are intersected before timing. The timed operation offsets that retained intersection by 1/100 with bevel corners.
benchmark_method.timed_scope: Fixture construction and the first capability probe are outside Runner timing. Runner performs one warm-up before every sample set.
benchmark_method.matched_control: Detached b9f0bf7 uses the identical 74-line benchmark patch, release settings, and dependency revisions and returns the same certified exact geometry.
benchmark_method.historical_control: Detached 3111455 uses the same benchmark patch but rejects the re-offset; its latency is capability context, not an equivalent performance baseline.
benchmark_method.competitive_control: Cavalier Contours performs the analogous binary64 polyline intersection fixture and bevel-like parallel offset. It has no selected fields, retained exact topology, or policy outcome and is a throughput sentinel only.
benchmark_method.perf_method: perf stat user-space instructions, cycles, branches, branch misses, and cache misses. The implementation-filter=disabled process retains fixture construction and the untimed capability probe. Current normalization divides the process difference by 257 warm-up/timed calls; b9f0bf7 normalization divides by two.
benchmark_method.heap_method: Heaptrack record-only runs 32 timed current operations plus the Runner warm-up. The disabled process retains fixture construction and the untimed capability probe; subtracting it and dividing by 33 reports operation allocation counts. Heaptrack wall time is not used.
benchmark_method.profile_method: Frame-pointer release perf records compare the correctness-equivalent semantic implementation and optimized implementation. Percentages are sampled-cycle attribution, not deterministic work counters.

matched_wall_performance.interpretation: The optimization comparison is correctness-equivalent and removes 99.85% of wall time. Historical rejection and Cavalier binary64 are explicitly non-equivalent context.

deterministic_perf.interpretation: The wall improvement is algorithmic: the operation retires about 16.27 million instructions instead of 18.47 billion.

allocation_evidence.parent_caveat: The parent 512-step refinement path becomes severely perturbed under Heaptrack, so its recorder wall time and incomplete matched subtraction are intentionally excluded. Wall and deterministic perf provide the parent comparison.
